title: Troy (Hisarlık)

place.label: Hisarlık mound, Çanakkale Province, Türkiye
place.basis: official UNESCO World Heritage point; not a boundary
place.coords_source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre official point for Archaeological Site of Troy (World Heritage List 849), published as N39 57 23.184 E26 14 20.4 at https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/849/maps/ (table read 2026-11-27); approximate, not a boundary

tiers.everyday: Troy is a mound of many cities built on top of each other in northwest Türkiye. It is generally believed to be the Troy of Homer's Iliad.
tiers.student: Pleiades records occupation at Ilion/Troia from an Early Bronze Age citadel in the 3rd millennium BC to the Roman period, and says the Hisarlık mound is generally believed to be Homer's Troy. UNESCO counts about 4,000 years of history, notes first excavations in 1870 and 24 excavation campaigns, and inscribed the site in 1998.

timeline.event: Early Bronze Age citadel (3rd millennium BC) begins the settlement
Inscribed on the World Heritage List

facts.label: Identification
facts.value: Generally believed to be Homer's Troy (Pleiades wording)

facts.label: Location
facts.value: Some 4.8 km off the Dardanelles' south mouth

unknowns: whether a Trojan War happened as told in the Iliad is not settled by our cited sources
